subject: EU renewal: SOC 2 re-attestation, log retention & auditor snapshot
messages:
From: Martin Weber <m.weber@europayments.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 Mar 2029 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Request: SOC2 re-attestation, EU log retention and auditor access

Hi Naomi,

Hope you’re doing well. Our renewal with Redwood is coming up in mid-May and our security team has flagged a few items that we need to confirm before we can sign:

- Retention horizon: we need logs retained for 36 months for specific EU payments flows (transaction and auth logs). Current contract references 24 months — can Redwood support a 36-month commit for those logs in the EU region?
- Auditor access: the external auditors want a weekend snapshot (read-only) of logs and system metadata for a one-off audit window. They prefer an isolated, auditable snapshot delivered over SFTP or a signed URL.
- Data residency and encryption: confirmation that KMS-managed keys used for EU workloads can be customer-managed and that rotation can be frozen for the audit window (we have strict key attestation requirements).

We’re also evaluating whether we should add a Dedicated pool for the audit period (to avoid noisy-neighbor risk). If Redwood has a short-term dedicated audit node offering (weekend or 7-day blocks) that would be ideal.

Can you point me to the operational steps, any pricing delta, and what evidence you’ll need from our side?

Thanks,
Martin Weber
Head of Security Operations
Europayments
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Martin Weber <m.weber@europayments.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 Mar 2029 10:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Request: SOC2 re-attestation, EU log retention and auditor access

Martin — thanks for the clear ask and the heads up about timing. Tagging Kimberly (account) and Connor (security ops) to scope the work. High-level answers below and a suggested path forward: 

1) Retention to 36 months: we can extend retention for the specified log classes in the EU region. This requires a contract amendment (short clause) plus a small storage surcharge; I’ve attached a manifest template so we can map which log streams you want in-scope.

2) Auditor snapshot: we can produce a read-only snapshot targeted to the log classes you list. Options:
  - Weekend single snapshot (one-time): create an immutable read-only archive and deliver via signed URL/SFTP.
  - 7-day audit window on a dedicated node: auditors hit a dedicated instance with read-only credentials; all access logs and session recordings are retained.

3) Customer-managed KMS: we support customer-provided keys in EU (bring-your-own-key). Connor — will confirm rotation freeze mechanics but in principle we can coordinate a freeze for the audit window with sufficient notice.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
- You confirm list of log classes and sample ranges (use attached manifest).
- Redwood prepares amendment + quote for 36-month retention and (a) one-time snapshot OR (b) 7-day dedicated audit node.
- Security pre-check: Connor to validate whether the snapshot requires a temporary IAM role or dedicated node.
- Target: sign amendment week of 2029-04-22 to schedule audit weekend in May.

I’ve attached the SOC2 evidence manifest template and a draft amendment for internal review. I’ll follow up with a short call invite once we have the log list.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Principal Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachments: SOC2_evidence_manifest.xlsx, redwood_amendment_draft.docx
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 Mar 2029 10:15:00 +0100
Subject: Fwd: Request: SOC2 re-attestation, EU log retention and auditor access

Kimberly / Connor — forwarding Martin’s note. Key asks: 36-month retention for specific EU logs, one-time weekend snapshot or 7-day dedicated node, customer-managed KMS freeze. Can you share rough cost delta and operational constraints? I put April 22 signing target on the timeline.

Quick priorities:
- Pricing for storage uplift to 36 months (per GB monthly incremental + one-time snapshot egress fee).
- Estimate for dedicated node (7-day block) cost and capacity if auditors may run queries.
- Any compliance gating (e.g., cross-region replication, PII redaction) that would prevent a straight snapshot.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate the external call once you confirm capacity.

— Naomi
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 Mar 2029 11:02:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: SOC2 re-attestation, EU log retention and auditor access

Naomi / Kim — quick technical read:

- Snapshot approach: feasible. For immutability and strong audit trail we’ll take these steps: create an immutable archive in the EU tenant, sign it with a snapshot digest, and publish an access bundle with ephemeral signed URLs. We’ll capture an audit runbook and session logs (we retain access logs for 90 days by default; note: we can extend that retention for the audit window).
- Dedicated node: we can spin a dedicated inference node in the EU for a 7-day block. If auditors will run heavy queries (replays, long tail analyses) we should provision additional GPU memory and isolate the KV cache. Estimate: baseline dedicated 1xV100-equivalent node for 7 days = EUR 5,800 (includes isolation + elevated logging).
- Storage uplift: 36-month retention for the specified log classes is straightforward; incremental storage delta depends on your average monthly ingress for those streams. If Martin can provide a 30-day sample (manifest), we’ll give a per-GB monthly surcharge and an egress schedule for the snapshot.
- KMS freeze: we can work with BYOK; rotation freeze requires an authorization ticket and a signed aging/rotation waiver. Need 72 hours lead time before the snapshot.

I’m attaching the audit runbook we use for previous EU audits (redacted). Also, we should surface this pricing to Commercial for a clean amendment.

Connor O'Brien
Security & Privacy Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: audit-runbook.pdf
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Martin Weber <m.weber@europayments.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 Mar 2029 11:45:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Request: SOC2 re-attestation, EU log retention and auditor access — proposed plan and next steps

Martin — thanks, all. Pulling together the specifics below so we can move to DocuSign: 

What Redwood will deliver:
- Contract amendment to extend retention to 36 months for the named log classes (will include a per-GB uplift).
- Option A: one-time immutable weekend snapshot delivered via signed URL (delivery egress fee applies).
- Option B: 7-day dedicated EU audit node with read-only auditor credentials, full session recording, and extended access logs (estimated cost: EUR 5,800).
- Support for customer-managed KMS; we require 72 hours notice to coordinate a rotation freeze.
- Audit runbook and sample manifest (attached).

What we need from Europayments:
- Completed SOC2_evidence_manifest.xlsx with the three example streams to be retained and a 30-day sample size.
- Decision on Option A or Option B.
- Signed amendment (I’ll send a DocuSign link).

Proposed schedule:
- 2029-04-08: Redwood sends final quote + amendment.
- 2029-04-22: Target signature.
- Audit weekend: target May 18–19 (flexible pending your auditor availability).

I’ve created a draft amendment and put the manifest template in the Drive folder (link below). When you send the completed manifest, Connor will produce the final storage and egress numbers and we’ll flow pricing to Commercial.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/link/ABCDEF-AMPLIFY-EOA
Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1EUropay-Audit-Sprint

Happy to jump on a 20-minute call Monday to review.

Best regards,
Naomi Feldman
Principal Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
